subject: Investigating dequeue lock-ups impacting Cartly peak traffic
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tina Lopez <tina@cartly.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High dequeue latency observed during Cartly evening peak

Team —

At ~08:45 PST we saw a sharp jump in dequeue/response latency for Cartly's GenAPI endpoint (their production traffic spiked ~3x). P95 increased from ~320ms to ~2s and several requests stalled for >5s. Platform metrics show a backlog forming on the inference queue and repeated worker restarts on node pool g-infer-07.

I attached a trimmed server log and a heap snapshot taken at 08:52. Initial notes:
- errors in logs: repeated "kv_cache_eviction" entries and a handful of OOM-adjacent GC spikes.
- topology: this is routed to shared-hosted pool with autoscaling; Cartly is on standard plan.

Immediate asks:
1) Ben — can you triage worker restarts and confirm whether kernel scheduling or allocator thrash is the root? If you need a jvm/heap-level dump from the model side, call it out.
2) Jonas — can you validate whether routing recently moved some Cartly traffic to the shared pool with lower memory headroom?
3) Marissa — product needs an external-facing short note for Cartly (one-paragraph) we can send while we investigate.

Impact: Cartly reports degraded quality of their checkout flows; they may throttle traffic if this persists. I've looped Tina for transparency.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- server-logs-2027-11-15.txt (text, 1.2MB)
- heap_snapshot-2027-11-15.zip (archive, 48MB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tina Lopez <tina@cartly.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High dequeue latency observed during Cartly evening peak

Thanks Grace — quick triage updates:
- I see the worker restarts; cause looks like memory pressure from a model variant that grew its KV cache size unexpectedly after a change in the sequence-length defaults two days ago.
- The autoscaler attempted to spin new pods but some hit node-level OOM eviction because our shared pool has a strict memory overcommit.
- No kernel panics; CPU steady. Mostly allocator/GPU memory residency churn.

Short-term mitigations I recommend right now:
1) Pause routing of new Cartly requests to pool g-infer-07 and route them to dedicated-fallback pool dfd-01 (lower throughput but stable memory headroom). I can flip routing policy now if we agree.
2) Apply a temporary per-request max_tokens cap (reduce KV footprint) — we can implement this at the gateway for Cartly for the next 30 minutes.
3) Roll back the sequence-length default change for the model family that serves Cartly; that requires a quick release from model-config but safe.

I can own 1 and 2. Need product sign-off on 3 (Marissa) because it is a change to model serving defaults.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

>

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tina Lopez <tina@cartly.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High dequeue latency observed during Cartly evening peak

Short answers and product asks:
- Agreed to the short-term mitigations Ben proposed — please route Cartly to dfd-01 and enable gateway token cap. Ben, when you flip routing, call out any expected request drop percentage.
- On the rollback: I want more context before we revert defaults. Questions for engineering: how many customers are on the affected model variant? Is this a change we pushed platform-wide two days ago? If the change is isolated to a small cohort, rolling back only for Cartly may be sufficient.

Customer comm draft (one paragraph) I propose we send to Tina and keep it simple:
"Tina — we observed a transient memory pressure event that increased response times for your GenAPI traffic during last night’s peak. We’ve routed your traffic to a stable fallback pool and applied a short-term cap to reduce memory pressure. We’re continuing a deeper investigation and will share a timeline for a permanent fix by EOD tomorrow. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you updated.

Please approve or suggest edits and I’ll send.

Product ask / roadmap question for engineering:
- If this is caused by sequence-length defaults increasing KV cache growth, we need a guardrail in the runtime: (a) reject or throttle requests that would exceed configured per-pod KV budget, and (b) an autoscaler signal that accounts for model KV state, not just memory RSS. Is there capacity to pull a short spike-proofing README into the roadmap? This is high priority for any multi-tenant customers.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Serving & Runtime
From: Tina Lopez <tina@cartly.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High dequeue latency observed during Cartly evening peak

Thanks for the quick heads up. Our checkout traffic spiked because we launched a promo at 09:30 PST and it exposed the degradation. Two quick asks from our side:
1) Can you share an ETA for the fallback routing and any expected impact on successful request rate? We need to decide whether to throttle the promo on our side.
2) If you think a rollback will be required, please say so — we can pause the promo for 30 minutes if that prevents customer-facing failures.

Appreciate transparency; we’ll stand by for your short customer note.

— Tina
Tina Lopez
Head of Engineering, Cartly
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tina Lopez <tina@cartly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Cartly incident update and next steps (routing + remediation plan)

Tina —

Thanks for the fast reply and for giving us time to coordinate. Short update and planned next steps (what we’ve done + what’s coming):

What we did (immediate):
- At 09:38 on Nov 15 we diverted Cartly traffic from g-infer-07 to dedicated-fallback pool dfd-01. Expected success rate impact: ~3–5% added latency on p50 (due to smaller pool) but near-zero error rate increase.
- Gateway per-request token cap applied (reduces average KV footprint by ~28%).
- We held off on a platform-wide rollback. Instead we scoped a rollback candidate to the affected model variant and prepared a canary release.

What we’re doing next (24–48h):
- Ben will run a controlled canary rollback to validate that sequence-length defaults are the root cause; canary targets non-production traffic and a single small production slice.
- Jonas and infra will add a short-term autoscaler tweak so node headroom is respected for KV cache growth; this is an operational config change (no code) and we expect it by EOD tomorrow.
- Product / Roadmap: Marissa will prepare a spec for runtime guardrails for KV budgets and an autoscaler signal for model state. We’ll prioritize this in the Q1 infra roadmap and tie it to a per-tenant protection flag.

Customer-facing note (the message we sent to Cartly at 09:50 on Nov 15):
"Tina — we observed a transient memory pressure event that increased response times for your GenAPI traffic during last night’s peak. We’ve routed your traffic to a stable fallback pool and applied a short-term cap to reduce memory pressure. We’re continuing a deeper investigation and will share a timeline for a permanent fix by EOD tomorrow. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you updated."

If you want a ticket with more detail (logs, timing, and mitigation steps) I can open a secured support link. Also, if you prefer we pause the promo window, say the word and we’ll wait on any canary rollback that might cause a brief risk.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
